subject: Hosted onramp: endpoints, rate limits, and networking checklist
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@cartflow.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted onramp: endpoints, rate limits, and networking checklist

Hi Maya — great to meet you on the demo earlier. Quick recap and a short checklist so we can scope a smooth hosted evaluation: 

Summary of what we demonstrated:
- Live demo of the Hosted API (generation + chat + embeddings)
- Canary fallback behavior and burst capacity demo
- Console walkthrough for per-token cost and trace logs

Questions / items we need from CartFlow to prepare the quickstart environment:
1) Traffic profile: estimated concurrent requests (p95 concurrency), average tokens per generation, and expected peak QPS per endpoint (for /generate vs /chat vs /embeddings).
2) Data residency / compliance constraints: are there any EU residency or retention windows beyond 30 days?
3) Testing endpoints: would you prefer us to provision dedicated test endpoints for the pilot, or use the shared sandbox with higher rate caps?
4) Networking: if you plan to test from your VPC or corporate IPs, please share a CIDR list for allowlisting (we can also support bringing a subset into VPC later).
5) Procurement / PO timeline and any required contract SLAs beyond our standard pilot terms.

Attached a short "Hosted Quickstart Checklist" (see attachment) that lists the exact artifacts we usually ask for. If you can reply with the traffic numbers and any procurement contact, we can provision the pilot endpoints and raise default rate caps for the test window.

Proposed next steps:
- You: reply with traffic/profile + procurement contact (today/this week)
- Us: provision endpoints & increase pilot rate caps (once traffic numbers received)
- Schedule 1-hour canary test run next week to validate latency and token costs

Thanks — I looped in Aditya (SE) to add technical notes.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Hosted-Quickstart-Checklist.pdf (1 page, PDF stub)

From: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@cartflow.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cartflow.ai>, Ankit Rao <ankit@cartflow.ai>
Date: 2027-03-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted onramp: endpoints, rate limits, and networking checklist

Hi Markus — thanks for the follow-up and the checklist. Quick answers below so you can size the pilot: 

Traffic profile (expected pilot load):
- Typical concurrency (p95): 12 concurrent requests
- Peak concurrency: 40 concurrent requests for short spikes (durations < 2 min)
- Average tokens per generation: ~180 tokens (customer-facing summaries)
- Embeddings usage: batch job overnight, ~10k embeddings/day, QPS during batch ~120
- Chat flows: a small set of users (beta) with multi-turn sessions averaging 8 turns

Data residency: US-only for now; no EU residency required for pilot. Retention: standard 30-day logs ok.

Networking: We'll run tests from our staging cluster (public IPs). I'll get you the static egress IPs — expect them by EOD. We are not ready to bring VPC/on-prem yet; hosted evaluation preferred to start.

Procurement: looping in procurement. We expect to sign pilot SOW by next Tuesday; budget approval in progress.

Can you confirm endpoint URLs and the default rate limits you set for pilots? Also interested in recommended request patterns to exercise KV-caching and batching.

Thanks,
Maya
Head of Product
CartFlow AI

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@cartflow.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-25T13:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted onramp: endpoints, rate limits, and networking checklist

Hi Maya — great profile, thanks. A few technical clarifications and notes on pilot defaults so you can plan load tests: 

Default pilot endpoints we typically provision:
- POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (single-turn generation)
- POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat (multi-turn chat with KV cache support)
- POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings (batch or single)

Pilot default rate caps (we can raise these for the scheduled window):
- Per-endpoint qps: 25 qps (soft limit)
- Burst capacity: up to 75 qps for short bursts (auto-throttles after 2 minutes)
- Concurrent request throttle (per-account): 60 concurrent requests by default

Token/latency notes:
- For generation with ~180 tokens, expect p50 latency ~220–350ms (model dependent), p95 ~600–900ms on Hosted shared pools; Dedicated reduces p95 by ~20–40% depending on model.
- Embeddings batch throughput is limited by batch size; use batches of 256–512 to maximize GPU utilization for the overnight job.

KV caching & batching guidance:
- To exercise KV caching in /chat, start with a short prefix warm-up (3 warm requests) so the model cache warms and subsequent multi-turn latency drops.
- For generation-heavy traffic, batching small requests (5–10 per batch) improves cost but increases tail latency; we can tune during the canary.

We can provision a temporary higher pilot cap for your canary window: suggest we set the per-endpoint qps to 100 and concurrent to 120 for the 2-hour run. Please confirm desired date/time and provide egress IPs for allowlist.

Attached a small sample of anonymized request logs to help you shape test traffic (sample-request-logs.jsonl). Also linking our quickstart doc: https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-quickstart that has curl examples and recommended payload shapes.

Next steps:
- Confirm canary window (preferred: Thu 2027-03-27 10:00–12:00 PT)
- Send static egress IPs for allowlisting
- Procurement: send PO contact and any contract SOW items to markus.klein@redwood.ai

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sample-request-logs.jsonl (JSONL stub)

If you prefer 10:00–12:00, we can shift — just let us know. We'll provision isolated pilot endpoints and temporarily raise the rate caps as Aditya indicated.

Thanks again — looking forward to the run.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
